observation.visible_scene: A seaside sunset view: the sun sits low on the horizon left of center, casting a bright shimmering reflection column across calm sea water. A dark headland/cliff topped by a light-colored building occupies the right side. A sloping sandy-pebbly beach fills the lower-right foreground, meeting a gentle surf line. The sky is overcast with layered gray clouds tinted by the low sun. The overall framing of the sun and cliff stays fixed throughout.
visible_changes: A long, low wave crest with a dark trough advances from mid-water toward the shore, becoming progressively more defined from roughly the middle of the excerpt onward.
As the wave reaches the beach, a band of white breaking foam forms and spreads diagonally across the lower-left/center shoreline, growing wider and moving closer to the foreground by the last frames.
The thin foam edge along the right side of the beach recedes and re-forms as the surf shifts.
The sun's reflection column on the water continuously shimmers and breaks into moving ripples, while the bright disc of the sun itself stays in the same position.
Small surface ripples across the open water subtly reorganize frame to frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the breaking wave fully runs up and back-washes after the last frame, and the longer-term sinking of the sun below the horizon.
The full wave period and any prior wave that set up the one seen advancing here.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is minimal/uncertain: the sun and cliff positions remain essentially constant, suggesting a static or near-static handheld shot rather than a deliberate pan.
The exact moment the wave begins to crest is gradual and not a sharp onset; it is an already-developing swell rather than a newly triggered event.
